intended_purpose: An implantable pulse generator intended to deliver electrical pacing therapy to sustain an adequate heart rhythm in patients with symptomatic bradycardia, implanted subcutaneously with transvenous leads to the myocardium.
device_description: Hermetically sealed titanium-housed implantable pulse generator with a 10-year battery life, connected to the heart via transvenous pacing leads, programmable via an external clinician programmer. Directly sustains a vital physiological function and is intended for long-term implantation.
clinical_data_summary: Pivotal clinical study (n=180, 24-month follow-up): primary endpoint of appropriate pacing capture met in 98.9% of patients; lead dislodgement rate 1.1%; no unanticipated device-related serious adverse events.
risk_summary: Risk management file per ISO 14971 identifies 41 hazards across electrical, mechanical, and biological categories, including hazards specific to long-term active implantation and life-sustaining failure modes. All residual risks rated acceptable after mitigation.

clinical_trial_data.trial_name: Pivotal study, n=180 (representative 10-patient sample shown here)
